references.text: Here the same officers (hypēretai) are described who were sent by the chief priests and Pharisees to arrest Jesus, but they return empty-handed with the words that never has any man spoken like this.
After Jesus performs a sign, the chief priests and Pharisees gather in council to plan his capture and death, a direct continuation of the attempt to seize him in chapter 7.
Jesus is finally arrested by a crowd that includes chief priests and officers (hypēretai) from the Pharisees, who carry out the arrest ordered earlier.
Another attempt by the chief priests and Pharisees to arrest Jesus, in which he escapes their grasp, shows the ongoing conflict and their repeated efforts to capture him.
The Pharisees acknowledge that the whole world has gone after Jesus, and express concern that they can no longer control the situation or arrest him without consequences.
